# @kernelui-lib/react — LLM reference

A component library built on real semantic HTML instead of div soup: every
component wraps a genuine native element (`<button>`, `<dialog>`, `<input
type="color">`, `<select>`...) or a documented WAI-ARIA pattern where no
native element exists (Tabs, Accordion's `<details>`, the combobox
pattern). If you already know HTML and ARIA, you already know most of the
behavior this library gives you — read this file once, then trust the
exported TypeScript types (`dist/index.d.ts`) for exact prop names.

## Install

```bash
npm install @kernelui-lib/react @kernelui-lib/styles
```

```tsx
import "@kernelui-lib/styles";        // tokens: color, radius, spacing, type
import "@kernelui-lib/react/styles.css"; // this package's compiled component CSS

import { Button, TextField } from "@kernelui-lib/react";
```

Both CSS imports are required for the library's actual visual design.
Skip `@kernelui-lib/react/styles.css` and every component still renders as its
real underlying element, fully functional, just unstyled — never broken.

## Conventions (true across nearly every component — learn these once)

- **Controlled/uncontrolled value**: `value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange`
  (not `onChange`, which is reserved for the native DOM event where a
  component also exposes one). Omit `value` and the component manages its
  own state; pass `value` + `onValueChange` to fully control it.
- **Form-field scaffold** (`TextField`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Combobox`,
  `TagInput`, `ColorPicker`, `FileUpload`, `NumberField`, `Slider`):
  `label` (required — the accessible name, always rendered as a real
  `<label>`), `hideLabel` (boolean — visually hides the label without
  removing it from the accessibility tree; `label` is still required when
  this is set), `description` (helper text), `errorMessage` (shown
  instead of `description`, with `role="alert"`, when `invalid` is true),
  `invalid` (boolean), `disabled`, `required`. Slot class hooks
  (`wrapperClassName`, `labelClassName`, `descriptionClassName`,
  `errorClassName`) and `data-focused`/`data-filled` support floating-label
  animations without targeting generated CSS-module class names.
- **Styling hooks**: `className` (on the actual interactive element,
  accepts a string or `(state) => string` for state-driven styling) and
  `wrapperClassName` (on the outer wrapper, same shape) where a component
  has both. Every component also forwards a `ref` to its real underlying
  DOM element via `forwardRef` — never a wrapper div.
- **Real elements, not ARIA-only**: don't add `role`/`aria-*` props that
  duplicate what the underlying native element already provides (e.g.
  don't add `role="button"` to `<Button>` — it's a real `<button>`).
- **No hidden global config**: every component takes its data via props,
  not a Provider you have to wrap the app in — the exceptions are
  `<ToastViewport>` (mount once, then call the imported `toast()`
  function from anywhere) and `<CommandPalette>` (same idea).
- **React and Web Components share one design**: `@kernelui-lib/elements`
  ships every component below as a framework-free Custom Element
  (`<kernel-button>`, `<kernel-text-field>`, ...) with the same visual
  design and equivalent kebab-case attributes (`onValueChange` becomes a
  `change` event with `event.detail`, boolean props become boolean
  attributes). Reach for it in Vue/Svelte/Astro/plain-HTML projects
  instead of this package.

## Components

### Primitives
- **Avatar** — Real image, with an initials fallback.
- **Badge** — A small status chip.
- **Button** — Click, keyboard, and form association, for free.
- **Checkbox** — Tri-state, styled with :checked and :indeterminate.
- **Label** — A standalone label for custom composed controls.
- **RadioGroup** (+ `RadioGroupItem`) — Grouped choice with native arrow-key roving.
- **Separator** — A divider that's already role="separator".
- **Switch** — The WAI-ARIA switch pattern on a real button.
- **Toggle** — A two-state toggle that looks and acts like a button.

### Forms
- **ColorPicker** — A real colour input, plus a typeable hex field on the same value.
- **Combobox** — Filterable list with aria-activedescendant.
- **FileUpload** — Drag-and-drop over a real file input, with optional square image preview moulding. `onError` fires with `type: "accept" | "max-size" | "max-files" | "directory"` when a pick or drop is rejected (including a dropped folder, which the platform surfaces as an unreadable 0-byte `File`).
- **InputOTP** — One-time-code entry with roving focus.
- **NumberField** — TextField's scaffold, specialised for numbers.
- **Select** (+ `SelectOption`) — The platform's own picker UI, on every device.
- **Slider** — Custom-painted thumb, native drag and keyboard behaviour.
- **TagInput** — Freeform text that commits into discrete, removable tags.
- **TextField** — Correct labelling and live validation styling.
- **Textarea** — Auto-growing with field-sizing: content.

### Layout
- **Card** (+ `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter`) — For genuinely self-contained, distributable content.
- **Footer** — The contentinfo landmark.
- **Header** — The banner landmark.
- **Nav** (+ `NavLink`) — Active state via aria-current, no client JS.
- **Resizable** — Pane-to-pane split layouts.
- **ScrollArea** — Custom scrollbar styling as enhancement only.
- **Sidebar** — The complementary landmark.

### Feedback
- **Callout** — Live-region feedback that announces itself.
- **Progress** — Reports its own value to assistive tech, natively.
- **Skeleton** — Loading placeholder tied to real content dimensions.
- **ToastViewport** (+ `toast`) — A shared, queued live region.

### Overlays
- **CommandPalette** — A searchable, keyboard-driven action list.
- **ContextMenu** — Right-click menu, same primitives as Dropdown Menu.
- **Dialog** — showModal(): focus trap, top layer, and ::backdrop, free.
- **DropdownMenu** (+ `DropdownMenuMorph`, `MenuItem`, `MenuSeparator`) — Anchor-positioned menu with arrow-key navigation. DropdownMenuMorph is an opt-in variant sharing MenuItem/MenuSeparator/MenuContext: the panel's own box animates width/height/border-radius out from the trigger's exact footprint (transitions.dev's "plus menu morph") instead of scaling/fading in place. It's popover="manual" rather than "auto" — a popover's hide can't be deferred, so the shrink-back-to-the-trigger close animation needs full manual control, with its own outside-click/Escape dismissal (same tradeoff ContextMenu/Combobox make). Elements: <kernel-dropdown-menu-morph>, same child shape as <kernel-dropdown-menu>.
- **HoverCard** — Rich hover preview, a heavier Tooltip.
- **NavigationMenu** (+ `NavigationMenuItem`, `NavigationMenuLink`, `NavigationMenuTrigger`, `NavigationMenuContent`) — Multi-level site navigation, mega-menu via popover.
- **Popover** — Anchor-positioned floating panel.
- **Sheet** (+ `useSheetDrag`) — A Dialog anchored to an edge, with drag-to-dismiss. Takes every Dialog prop, with `side` narrowed to bottom/top/left/right and defaulting to `"bottom"`. Adds `showHandle`, `handleOnly` (restricts dragging to the handle and footer; set it when the body scrolls), `dismissible` (disables dragging and backdrop dismissal, not Escape), `closeThreshold`, `velocityThreshold`, `onDrag`, `onRelease`, `inset` (detached and floating, all four corners rounded), `maxDisplayWidth` (closes itself above that viewport width), and `footer` (pinned below the scrolling body; it owns the bottom safe area and is a drag surface). A gesture that starts by scrolling the body hands over to the sheet mid-drag once the scroller reaches its edge. `snapPoints` (viewport percentages along the axis the sheet grows — dvh for bottom/top, dvw for left/right, and it works on every side) gives it resting sizes with `snap`/`defaultSnap`/`onSnapChange`: a flick steps exactly one snap, a slower release lands on the nearest, and dragging below the smallest dismisses. Snap settles are carried by a real spring so they leave at the speed the finger was moving; pass `spring={false}` for a CSS transition, or `{ attraction, friction }` to tune.
- **Tooltip** — Hover/focus hints via the Popover API.

### Navigation
- **Breadcrumbs** (+ `BreadcrumbItem`, `BreadcrumbsTrail`) — Ordered trail, aria-current for the current page.
- **Pagination** (+ `PaginationItem`, `PaginationPrevious`, `PaginationNext`, `PaginationEllipsis`) — Ordered page links, aria-current for the active one.
- **Tabs** (+ `TabsList`, `Tab`, `TabPanel`) — No native element exists yet, ARIA APG pattern.

### Data Display
- **Accordion** (+ `AccordionItem`) — Native disclosure, exclusive open via a shared name.
- **Carousel** (+ `CarouselSlide`) — Native scrolling instead of a JS carousel engine.
- **DataTable** — Table plus the behaviour layered on top.
- **DatePicker** — Calendar grid with aria-selected.
- **DateRangePicker** — Two-click range selection over the same calendar grid.
- **Table** (+ `TableCaption`, `TableHeader`, `TableBody`, `TableRow`, `TableHead`, `TableCell`) — Sortable headers, real <caption>, real <th scope>.

### AI
- **AgentActivity** (+ `AgentActivityItem`) — One chronological stream of reasoning, searches, tool calls, and traces. AgentActivityItem takes kind ("reasoning" | "search" | "tool" | "trace"), status ("pending" | "running" | "complete" | "error"), and label. Reasoning and tool steps delegate their body to the existing Reasoning and ToolCall components rather than reimplementing disclosure and status behaviour, so those two stay the single source of truth (and stay usable standalone). Search and trace steps render their own <details>. A step with no children is a plain status line.
- **CodeBlock** (+ `linesFromCode`, `linesText`) — A code surface with line numbers, copy, and stable streaming. Highlights nothing itself: pass pre-tokenised lines (CodeLine[] from utils/codeTokens.ts — { tokens: [{ text, className?, color? }] }) from Shiki/Prism/your own highlighter, or a plain `code` string for un-highlighted source. That's what keeps both packages dependency-free. Lines are keyed by index so appending streamed output updates the last line in place instead of re-mounting the ones above it, which is what avoids flicker and lost text selection. Line numbers are aria-hidden and unselectable so a copy contains code, not gutter. Following the live edge while `streaming` reuses StickToBottomController. In the elements package, content arrives via the `lines` or `code` DOM property, with light-DOM <pre><code> as the progressive-enhancement fallback.
- **Composer** — A chat message input, with a live "thinking" state.
- **FileDiff** — File changes as a real table, with live counts and progressive rows. rows is DiffRow[]: { kind: "add" | "remove" | "context" | "hunk", oldLine?, newLine?, content?, tokens? } — tokens are the same CodeToken shape CodeBlock takes. A diff is tabular data, so it's a <table> with line numbers in their own cells; copying a diff copies the code, not the gutter. The +/− marker is real text, never colour alone. `streaming` holds the disclosure open while rows arrive; with collapseOnComplete it settles closed ~600ms after streaming ends, and only on that edge, so a manual re-open is never overridden. In the elements package rows arrive via the `rows` DOM property.
- **MessageList** (+ `Message`, `MessageBubble`) — Conversation rows: authored, grouped, aligned, optionally expandable. MessageList renders the <ol>; Message renders one <li> wrapping an <article> (so screen readers can jump message to message), taking author ("user" | "assistant" | "system"), avatar, name, metadata, grouped, live, animateOnMount. MessageBubble is the surface, with tone ("neutral" | "accent" | "muted" | "danger"), align ("start" | "center" | "end"), and expandable, which renders a real <details> rather than a max-height clamp. The mount-only enter animation is a CSS keyframe animation, so re-rendering a transcript never re-animates its history. In the elements package an avatar is a child marked data-slot="avatar".
- **MessageScroller** (+ `useStickToBottom`, `StickToBottomController`) — Follows streamed output at the live edge, and lets go when the reader scrolls away. Pinning is deliberately not a controlled prop — it answers "is the reader at the bottom?", which only the DOM knows. Seed it with defaultPinned and observe it with onPinnedChange. The behaviour core is StickToBottomController (also exported, plus the useStickToBottom hook), which derives pin state from scroll position alone and flags its own programmatic scrolls. Pass conversationKey to re-arm the viewport when swapping transcripts.
- **Reasoning** — A collapsible AI reasoning trace that auto-opens while streaming.
- **Sources** (+ `Source`, `Citation`) — Cited sources and inline numbered citation chips for grounded answers.
- **Suggestion** (+ `SuggestionItem`) — Prompt suggestion chips that seed the next composer message.
- **ThinkingIndicator** — The universal typing-indicator dots, next to real visible text.
- **TodoList** (+ `TodoItem`) — An agent's task plan, with cross-fading status marks and a live completion count. TodoItem takes status ("pending" | "active" | "done" | "error"), metadata, and statusLabel. All four status marks render at once and cross-fade on data-status, so a status change is one attribute write with no JS in the transition. Every item also carries its status as visually hidden text — the mark is never the only signal. TodoList derives its completion count from direct TodoItem children; pass completed/total explicitly when the items are nested inside your own wrappers. The custom element recomputes the count from a MutationObserver on child status attributes.
- **ToolCall** — Collapsible agent tool status with pending, running, complete, and error states.
<!-- GENERATED:COMPONENTS:END -->

## Utilities

- **`useDetailsTransition()`** / **`DetailsPanelAnimator`** — The measured-height
  open/close motion behind `Accordion`, `Reasoning` and `ToolCall`, exported for
  building your own `<details>` disclosure with the same feel. The hook returns
  `{ detailsRef, contentRef, open, setOpen }`: put `detailsRef` on a `<details>`,
  `contentRef` on a single wrapper element holding everything except the
  `<summary>`. Accepts `defaultOpen` / `open` / `onOpenChange` (controlled or
  uncontrolled). It drives the panel from `click` on the `<summary>` rather than
  the `toggle` event, because `toggle` is non-cancelable and fires only *after*
  the browser has already painted the panel at full height. Honours
  `prefers-reduced-motion` by snapping, and sets `data-state="opening"` /
  `"closing"` on the `<details>` while in flight. Use `DetailsPanelAnimator`
  directly outside React.
- **`renderElement`**, **`resolveClassName`**, **`dataAttr`**, **`mergeRefs`** —
  The polymorphic/`className` helpers the components themselves use.

## Where to look for exact prop types

This file is a map, not the source of truth. For exact prop names,
types, and defaults: read `dist/index.d.ts` in this package (every prop
has a JSDoc comment explaining the *why*, not just the type) — or, if
this package was installed alongside the project's docs site, every
component has a live Playground and a machine-readable markdown mirror
at `/components/<slug>.md` (and one combined `/llms-full.txt` for the
whole library, plus `/registry.json` for structured metadata) generated
from the same pages a human would read.
